title: Chapter 25. Appendix. Padas signed "Narahari" from the Gaura-pada-tarangini — IX: Advaita
html:
Continuation of the appendix (the introductory note on the two Naraharis, on the arguments for attribution and on the marks in the headings is in ch. 17). Chapter 25: GPT section 6.2 "Advaita" (GPT1 pp. 439–449) — all fourteen padas signed Narahari (nos. 5–7, 9–11, 13, 15–18, 20, 21, 24): Advaita among Gaura's companions in the morning at Navadvipa, His form, His thundering calls and His dancing in the kirtana of Gaura's glories, a survey of His life, a praise, and His advent at Navagram. The signatures of the section were checked throughout, in the OCR and on the scan; the 12th wave of the Bhakti-ratnakara (BR) at the relevant places, the Gaura-charita-chintamani (GCC, kirana 4) and the section on Advaita in the Gita-chandrodaya were read continuously. Not translated (outside the appendix): nos. 8, 12, 14, 19, 22, 23 — signed Ghanashyama; no. 4 — no signature (it ends "the Lord Sankarshana wanders behind them from door to door"); the other padas of the section are by other poets (Vrindavana Dasa, Lochana, Shyamadasa, Vaishnava Dasa, Kanu, Trilochana, Gokulananda, Balarama Dasa). The base text is GPT1 (doubtful places by the scan), collated with GPT2, the GCC (ed. 1947), the BR (eds. 1912 and 1960) and the Gita-chandrodaya; the PK, KGC and PS were checked. Advaita Acharya is Maha-Vishnu Himself and Sadashiva, non-different from Hari (CC Adi 6; the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika, 11, 76, also calls Him Sadashiva); as with Gaura and Nityananda, the pronouns referring to Him are capitalized. The notes of the GPT editors are not reproduced.

1. Narahari — "rajanī prabhāta prabhākara sama…" (GPT1 p. 440, section 6.2, no. 5; GCC)

Morning among the companions: seeing the rising of Gaura's moon-face, Advaita, shining like the sun, beats His armpits in jubilation, walks to and fro more intoxicated than the king of elephants; His smile is a rain of jasmine; tears flow from His eyes like strings of pearls. Raga beloyara. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.1

রজনী প্রভাত প্রভাকর সম অদ্বৈত মহাশয় পরম উলাস ।
করত কক্ষযুগ-বাদ্য নিরন্তর নিরখি গৌর-মুখচন্দ্র প্রকাশ ॥

rajanī prabhāta prabhākara sama advaita mahāśaya parama ulāsa |
karata kakṣayuga-bādya nirantara nirakhi gaura-mukhacandra prakāśa ||

rajanī prabhāta — the night has turned to dawn; prabhākara sama — like the sun; advaita mahāśaya — Advaita Mahashaya; parama ulāsa — in supreme delight; karata — makes; kakṣayuga-bādya — the beating of both armpits; nirantara — ceaselessly; nirakhi — seeing; gaura-mukhacandra — of Gaura's moon-face; prakāśa — the rising

1.1The night has turned to dawn — and Advaita Mahashaya, like the sun, in supreme delight, ceaselessly beats His armpits, seeing the rising of Gaura's moon-face.

তুন্দিল দেহ দিশা-জয়কৃত অতি শোভিত তহি নব পুলক বিরাজ ।
ইতি উতি করত গতাগতি অদভুত অধিক মত্ত জিতি কুঞ্জররাজ ॥

tundila deha diśā-jayakṛta ati śobhita tahi naba pulaka birāja |
iti uti karata gatāgati adabhuta adhika matta jiti kuñjararāja ||

tundila deha — the portly body; diśā-jaya-kṛta — that has conquered the quarters; ati śobhita — is most beautiful; tahi — on it; naba pulaka birāja — fresh horripilation shines; iti uti — here and there; karata gatāgati — He goes to and fro; adabhuta — wondrously; adhika matta — more intoxicated; jiti — surpassing; kuñjara-rāja — the king of elephants

1.2His portly body, which has conquered the quarters, is most beautiful, and on it shines fresh horripilation; wondrously He walks to and fro, more intoxicated than the king of elephants.

লহু লহু হসত লসত দশনাবলী শ্বেত কিরণ নিকসত অনিবার ।
অপরূপ কুন্দকুসুম চহুঁ দিশ বুঝি বরষত সুঘর লোভ রিঝ আর ॥

lahu lahu hasata lasata daśanābalī śveta kiraṇa nikasata anibāra |
aparūpa kundakusuma cahum̐ diśa bujhi baraṣata sughara lobha rijha āra ||

lahu lahu hasata — He laughs softly; lasata daśanābalī — the rows of teeth gleam; śveta kiraṇa — white rays; nikasata anibāra — issue ceaselessly; aparūpa — wondrous; kunda-kusuma — jasmine flowers; cahum̐ diśa — in all directions; bujhi — as if; baraṣata — rain down; sughara — the connoisseurs; lobha — longing; rijha — delight; āra — and more

1.3He laughs softly — His rows of teeth gleam, white rays issue ceaselessly, as if wondrous jasmine flowers were raining down on every side, — and the connoisseurs of beauty are filled with longing and delight.

টলমল নয়নযুগল জল ছলছল চরত চারু বারণ নাহি মানি ।
মুকুতাদাম সদৃশ করু ঝলমল নরহরি পহুঁক পরাভব জানি ॥

ṭalamala nayanayugala jala chalachala carata cāru bāraṇa nāhi māni |
mukutādāma sadṛśa karu jhalamala narahari pahum̐ka parābhaba jāni ||

ṭalamala — tremble; nayana-yugala — both eyes; jala chalachala — brimming with tears; carata cāru — flow beautifully; bāraṇa nāhi māni — heeding no restraint; mukutādāma sadṛśa — like strings of pearls; karu jhalamala — glitter; narahari — Narahari; pahum̐ka — of the Lord; parābhaba — the victory over [them]; jāni — knows

1.4His eyes tremble, brimming with tears, and the tears flow beautifully, heeding no restraint, glittering like strings of pearls, — and Narahari sees the pearls put to shame by the Lord.2

GCC — kirana 4 ("the Lord among His devotees": in the morning, after waking, the companions gather round Gaura, and the poet describes each of them — Nityananda, padas 7–11, Advaita, padas 12–15, Gadadhara, 16–17, Narahari Sarakara, 18, Srivasa, 19, and others), pada 12 ("punaḥ beloyāra"; right after the pada on Nityananda's form — no. 29 of chapter 24). Readings: 1.1 "nirakhi" ("seeing") — from the GCC, the word has dropped out in the GPT (the line is short of the metre); 1.4 GCC "calata" ("flow"; GPT "carata"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya. B. Note 57 of chapter 24 wrongly calls this pada no. 4 (corrected). arms, and Kali trembles at Advaita's roar). "Portly body": in the lila Advaita is the elder, venerable in years (cf. "the old man", buṛā, in other poets of the same section); "which has conquered the quarters" — by its radiance and might. Advaita's tears and laughter are the ecstasy of love for Gaura, whom He Himself called into the world. The last words (pahum̐ka parābhaba jāni, lit. "knows the defeat by the Lord") may also be understood otherwise: "Narahari owns himself defeated by the Lord's beauty".

2. Narahari — "sītāpati atiśaya sukhe bhora…" (GPT1 p. 441, no. 6; GCC)

Advaita, the Lord of Sita, is absorbed in happiness and reflects with a smile: Gaura's beauty has left Madana no trace of pride; the three worlds, having drunk this intoxicating nectar, have forgotten everything and made Shachi's son the essence of their life; the word "sorrow" has vanished; the sin of Kali with its retinue is cowed. Raga not specified ("yathārāga"). Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.3

সীতাপতি অতিশয় সুখে ভোর ।
মনহি বিচার করত মৃদু হসি হসি ঐছে মদন-মদ ন রহল থোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

sītāpati atiśaya sukhe bhora |
manahi bicāra karata mṛdu hasi hasi aiche madana-mada na rahala thora || dhru ||

sītāpati — the Lord of Sita; atiśaya sukhe bhora — absorbed in boundless happiness; manahi — in His mind; bicāra karata — reflects; mṛdu hasi hasi — smiling gently; aiche — thus; madana-mada — of Madana's pride; na rahala thora — not a little remained

2.1The Lord of Sita is absorbed in boundless happiness.
Smiling gently, He reflects in His mind: "Thus not a little of Madana's pride is left!"

অতি অপরূপ ইহ গৌরবরণ বর মাদক অমৃত অলপ করি পান ।
মাতল ত্রিজগত সকল বিসারল সার করল শচীতনয় পরাণ ॥

ati aparūpa iha gaurabaraṇa bara mādaka amṛta alapa kari pāna |
mātala trijagata sakala bisārala sāra karala śacītanaya parāṇa ||

ati aparūpa — most wondrous; iha — this; gaura-baraṇa bara — excellent golden complexion; mādaka amṛta — intoxicating nectar; alapa kari pāna — drinking a little; mātala trijagata — the three worlds became intoxicated; sakala bisārala — forgot everything; sāra karala — made the essence; śacī-tanaya — Shachi's son; parāṇa — of their life

2.2How wondrous is this excellent golden complexion — an intoxicating nectar: drinking only a little of it, the three worlds became intoxicated, forgot everything and made Shachi's son the essence of their life.

জনমন-প্রবল তাপ তম হারণ করুণালয় সুপারিষদ চন্দ ।
দুঃখ শবদ মহি হোত শ্রবণগত ভবন ভুবন মধি অধিক আনন্দ ॥

janamana-prabala tāpa tama hāraṇa karuṇālaya supāriṣada canda |
duḥkha śabada mahi hota śrabaṇagata bhabana bhubana madhi adhika ānanda ||

janamana — of people's hearts; prabala tāpa — the fierce burning; tama — the darkness; hāraṇa — removing; karuṇālaya — abode of compassion; supāriṣada — with fine companions; canda — the moon; duḥkha śabada — the word "sorrow"; mahi — on earth; hota śrabaṇa-gata — has gone from hearing; bhabana bhubana madhi — in homes and in the worlds; adhika ānanda — great bliss

2.3The Moon with His fine companions, the abode of compassion, takes away the fierce burning and the darkness of people's hearts; the word "sorrow" has gone from hearing on earth, in homes and in all the worlds there is great bliss.

মিটল হরষ বিপরীত ভেল অব পরিকর সহ কুণ্ঠিত কলিপাপ ।
হরি হরি কো অধিকার হীন করু নরহরি ভণ পহুঁ তব পরতাপ ॥

miṭala haraṣa biparīta bhela aba parikara saha kuṇṭhita kalipāpa |
hari hari ko adhikāra hīna karu narahari bhaṇa pahum̐ taba paratāpa ||

miṭala haraṣa — the joy ended; biparīta bhela — everything turned the other way; aba — now; parikara saha — with its retinue; kuṇṭhita — cowed; kali-pāpa — the sin of Kali; hari hari — Hari, Hari; ko — whom; adhikāra hīna karu — has it not stripped of power; narahari bhaṇa — Narahari says; pahum̐ — O Lord; taba paratāpa — Your might

2.4[Kali's] joy has ended, everything has turned the other way: now the sin of Kali with all its retinue is cowed. Hari, Hari! Whom has it not stripped of power, — says Narahari, — Your might, O Lord!4

pada 13 ("yathārāga"). Readings: 2.1 "bicāra" ("reflects") — from the GCC (GPT1 and GPT2 misprint "bicā"); 2.3 GCC "bharala bhubanamadhi adhika ānanda" ("great bliss filled the worlds"; GPT "bhavana bhuvana madhi"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya. B. "the enchanter of Madana": this is praise of the Lord's all-attractive beauty, not of worldly attraction. "The Moon" is Gaura (Gaurachandra) with His companions. Kali is the personified age of quarrel; his "joy" is his power over people, which the advent of the Lord and of His name destroys.

3. Narahari — "acyuta-janaka janāśraya jagamadhi…" (GPT1 p. 441, no. 7; GCC)

The Father of Achyuta, stirred by longings, with a pauper's greed takes Gaura, still in His night attire, through His eyes into His heart, worships Him with the flowers of His bhavas, dances unnoticed crying "Jaya!" and repeats: "I have won!"; Narahari, Haridasa and the others watch Him in unspeakable happiness. Raga not specified. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the GCC; Vrajabuli.5

অচ্যুত-জনক জনাশ্রয় জগমধি বিদিত উদার দীন-দুঃখহারী ।
করতহি কত কত মনহি মনোরথ অধীর হোত পুন রহত সম্ভারী ॥

acyuta-janaka janāśraya jagamadhi bidita udāra dīna-duḥkhahārī |
karatahi kata kata manahi manoratha adhīra hota puna rahata sambhārī ||

acyuta-janaka — the Father of Achyuta; janāśraya — the shelter of people; jagamadhi bidita — renowned in the world; udāra — generous; dīna-duḥkha-hārī — remover of the sorrow of the lowly; karatahi — He forms; kata kata — so many; manahi — in His mind; manoratha — longings; adhīra hota — loses composure; puna — again; rahata sambhārī — restrains Himself

3.1The Father of Achyuta, shelter of people, renowned in the world, generous, remover of the sorrow of the lowly, forms so many longings in His mind — now He loses composure, now again restrains Himself.

প্রবল লোভ রঙ্ক সম নিঃশঙ্কহি রজনীক বেশ সহিত দ্বিজরাজ ।
লোচন পন্থে লেই বহু যতনহি বৈঠায়ল হিয়-আসন মাঝ ॥

prabala lobha raṅka sama niḥśaṅkahi rajanīka beśa sahita dvijarāja |
locana panthe lei bahu yatanahi baiṭhāyala hiya-āsana mājha ||

prabala lobha — with fierce greed; raṅka sama — like a pauper; niḥśaṅkahi — without hesitation; rajanīka beśa sahita — in His night attire; dvijarāja — the king of the twice-born (the moon); locana-panthe — by the path of the eyes; lei — taking; bahu yatanahi — with great care; baiṭhāyala — seated; hiya-āsana mājha — on the throne of His heart

3.2With the unbounded greed of a pauper, without hesitation, the King of the twice-born — still in His night attire — He took in by the path of the eyes and with great care seated on the throne of His heart.

ভাব-কদম্ব-কুসুম দেই পূজত তনু মন নিরমঞ্ছন করু তায় ।
জয় জয় শবদ উচরি অলখিত মৃদু নাচত জন মন লেত চোরায় ॥

bhāba-kadamba-kusuma dei pūjata tanu mana niramañchana karu tāya |
jaya jaya śabada ucari alakhita mṛdu nācata jana mana leta corāya ||

bhāba-kadamba-kusuma — kadamba flowers of bhava; dei — offering; pūjata — He worships; tanu mana — body and mind; niramañchana karu tāya — offers to Him in nirmanchana; jaya jaya śabada uccari — crying "jaya, jaya"; alakhita — unnoticed; mṛdu nācata — dances gently; jana mana — people's hearts; leta corāya — steals away

3.3He worships Him, offering kadamba flowers — His bhavas, and offers body and mind to Him in nirmanchana; crying "Jaya, jaya!", unnoticed, He dances gently — and steals away people's hearts.

খণে খণে জিতলুঁ জিতলুঁ বলি প্রফুল্লিত আপহি আপ দরশরস ভোর ।
অনুপম ভঙ্গী নিরখি নরহরি হরিদাস আদি সুখ কো করু ওর ॥

khaṇe khaṇe jitalum̐ jitalum̐ bali praphullita āpahi āpa daraśarasa bhora |
anupama bhaṅgī nirakhi narahari haridāsa ādi sukha ko karu ora ||

khaṇe khaṇe — again and again; jitalum̐ jitalum̐ bali — saying "I have won, I have won"; praphullita — blossoming; āpahi āpa — by Himself; daraśa-rasa bhora — absorbed in the rasa of beholding; anupama bhaṅgī — the matchless gestures; nirakhi — seeing; narahari haridāsa ādi — Narahari, Haridasa and the others; sukha — of the happiness; ko karu ora — who can find the end

3.4Again and again He says: "I have won, I have won!" — and blossoms, absorbed by Himself in the rasa of beholding. Seeing this matchless play, Narahari, Haridasa and the others — who can measure their happiness?6

(pada 15) comes Ghanashyama's pada on Advaita's form (GPT no. 8). Readings: 3.2 "raṅka sama" ("like a pauper") and "rajanīka beśa" ("night attire"; cf. in the same kirana, pada 16: the Lord in the morning "in His night dress") — from the GCC; the GPT "bakṣa sama", "rajanī kareṇa" make no sense; 3.4 GCC "ko kahu ora" ("who can tell"). Not in the BR, PK, KGC, PS, Gita-chandrodaya. B. Infallible" (Krishna). The King of the twice-born (dvijarāja) is both the moon and the king of brahmanas: Gaura. Nirmanchana is the rite of circular offering (as in arati), a sign of self-surrender. "I have won!": Advaita triumphs — His worship has been fulfilled, the Lord whom He called has appeared (cf. in the same GPT section Lochana's pada no. 30: "jitilum̐ jitilum̐… jība nistārite habe gaura abatāra"). In the last line the name "Narahari" is both the poet's signature and, probably, the name of one of the onlookers: in the same kirana of the GCC, the pada after those on Advaita and Gadadhara (pada 18) praises Narahari Sarakara among the Lord's companions; Haridasa is Haridasa Thakura.

4. Narahari — "śrī-advaitacandra bhūpa mora…" (GPT1 p. 442, no. 9; BR; GCd)

Advaita's form in love for Gaura: tears from His reddened eyes, a radiance shaming hosts of suns, a gait surpassing the elephant's, a smile; His roar robs the lion of its pride — Kali trembles, the wicked flee; the ocean of compassion overflows and the fallen float in the rasa of bhakti. Raga kamoda or belavali. Attribution: probably Chakravarti — the pada is in the BR and the Gita-chandrodaya; Vrajabuli.7

শ্রীঅদ্বৈতচন্দ্র ভূপ মোর ।
গৌরপ্রেমভরে গর গর অন্তর অবিরত অরুণ-নয়ানে ঝরে লোর ॥ ধ্রু ॥

śrīadvaitacandra bhūpa mora |
gaurapremabhare gara gara antara abirata aruṇa-nayāne jhare lora || dhru ||

śrī-advaitacandra — Sri Advaitachandra; bhūpa mora — my sovereign; gaura-prema-bhare — with the weight of love for Gaura; gara gara antara — His heart overflowing; abirata — ceaselessly; aruṇa-nayāne — from His reddened eyes; jhare lora — tears stream

4.1Sri Advaitachandra is my sovereign!
His heart overflows with love for Gaura, tears stream ceaselessly from His reddened eyes.

পুলকিত ললিত অঙ্গ ঝলমল কত দিনকর-নিকর নিন্দি বর জ্যোতি ।
কুঞ্জরগমন দমন মনোরঞ্জন হসত সুলসত দশন জনু মোতি ॥

pulakita lalita aṅga jhalamala kata dinakara-nikara nindi bara jyoti |
kuñjaragamana damana manorañjana hasata sulasata daśana janu moti ||

pulakita — thrilled with horripilation; lalita aṅga — graceful limbs; jhalamala — shine; kata — how; dinakara-nikara — hosts of suns; nindi — putting to shame; bara jyoti — with excellent light; kuñjara-gamana damana — surpassing the elephant's gait; manorañjana — delighting the heart; hasata — He laughs; sulasata daśana — His teeth gleam; janu moti — like pearls

4.2His graceful limbs, thrilling with horripilation, shine with an excellent light that puts to shame hosts of suns; His gait, the delight of the heart, surpasses the elephant's; He laughs — and His teeth gleam like pearls.

সিংহগরবহর গরজত ঘন ঘন কম্পিত কলি দূরে দুরজন গেল ।
প্রবল প্রতাপে তাপত্রয় কুণ্ঠিত জগজন পরম হরিষহিয়া ভেল ॥

siṃhagarabahara garajata ghana ghana kampita kali dūre durajana gela |
prabala pratāpe tāpatraya kuṇṭhita jagajana parama hariṣahiyā bhela ||

siṃha-garaba-hara — robbing the lion of its pride; garajata ghana ghana — He roars again and again; kampita kali — Kali trembles; dūre durajana gela — the wicked have fled far; prabala pratāpe — by His mighty power; tāpatraya — the threefold miseries; kuṇṭhita — are subdued; jagajana — the people of the world; parama hariṣa-hiyā bhela — became supremely glad at heart

4.3Robbing the lion of its pride, He roars again and again — Kali trembles, the wicked flee far away; by His mighty power the threefold miseries are subdued, and the hearts of the people are filled with supreme gladness.

করুণা-জলধি উমড়ি চহুঁ দিশ পামর পতিত ভকতিরসে ভাসি ।
নরহরি কুমতি কি বুঝব রঙ্গ নব গৌরচরিত গুণ ভুবনে প্রকাশি ॥

karuṇā-jaladhi umaṛi cahum̐ diśa pāmara patita bhakatirase bhāsi |
narahari kumati ki bujhaba raṅga naba gauracarita guṇa bhubane prakāśi ||

ed. 1960, vv. 1763–1766, "punaḥ — bhūpālī"): Ishana, showing Srinivasa the places of Navadvipa, tells how the Lord sent Rama Pandita to Shantipura for Advaita, and from there turns to Advaita's family: His father is Kuvera Pandita (a quotation from the Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika on Kubera, v. 1755), His mother Nabha; in their old age Advaitachandra was born to them at Navagram (vv. 1751–1758); then comes Ghanashyama's pada on the advent (GPT no. 23, vv. 1759–1762) and this one; after it — "at Advaita's birth all loudly sang the names of Krishna and Govinda", His childhood, the move to Shantipura, His marriage (v. 1767 ff.). Readings: 14.1 BR "prakaṭi'" ("appearing"); 14.2 BR "biloki" ("seeing"); 14.4 BR "janama-bilāsa". The Navadvipa-parikrama is the same as the BR. Not in the PK, KGC, PS, GCC, Gita-chandrodaya. B. Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika (81–85) Kubera received from Sadashiva the boon: "in another birth I shall become your son". The Lord's appearance is not subject to the laws of karma: it is a descent, not the birth of a conditioned soul (cf. Bhagavad-gita 4.6–9). "Thaita taka taka thona" are rhythm syllables (bol) of the dance.
